Prince of Life
prins uhv lyf
noun
From Acts 3:15; a title of Christ as the Author and Originator of life, whom men killed yet God raised.

Biblical Definition

The Prince of life is a title of the Lord Jesus Christ given by Peter in his sermon at the temple gate: And killed the Prince of life, whom God hath raised from the dead; whereof we are witnesses. The word translated Prince means the author, the originator, the captain, the one who leads and from whom a thing proceeds; Christ is the Prince of life as the very Author and Source of life, both the natural life by which all things live and move and have their being, and the eternal life He gives to His people. The title carries a sharp and holy irony, which Peter presses upon his hearers: they killed the Prince of life—the very Author of life put to death by His creatures; yet death could not hold its Lord, and God raised Him from the dead. The One who is life cannot be conquered by death; rather, by His death and rising He has abolished death and brought life and immortality to light. He has the keys of death and of hell, and gives eternal life to whomsoever He will. The dictionary honors Christ as the Prince of life—the Author of all life, whom wicked hands crucified, but whom God raised, the conqueror of death and the giver of life to His people—and presses the same wonder Peter pressed: that men should kill the Author of life, and that the slain Prince should rise to give life to His murderers who repent.

Modern Corruption

Christ’s title is dimmed to mere honorific; Scripture proclaims Him the very Author of life, slain yet risen, the conqueror of death and giver of eternal life.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The corruption is the dimming of the title into a mere honorific—Prince of life as a pious flourish—losing the staggering claim it makes. Peter does not flatter; he confronts. He charges his hearers that they killed the Prince of life (Acts 3:15): the very Author of life, the One in whom was life and the life was the light of men (John 1:4), was put to death by the creatures who owed Him their every breath. The title is a thunderclap, not an ornament.

The principle to recover is the deity and life-giving power of Christ, vindicated in His resurrection. The Author of life could not be held by death; God raised Him, and He is alive for evermore, holding the keys of hell and of death (Rev 1:18). He is Himself the resurrection and the life (John 11:25), and gives eternal life to whom He will. The wonder Peter pressed remains: that men should murder the Prince of life, and that the slain Prince should rise to offer life to His very murderers, if they repent. To confess Christ as the Prince of life is to bow before Him as the divine Source of all life and the conqueror of the grave.
